body.en:
> Interviewer asks: "A team changed the serving stack for an internal draft assistant. Mean latency fell from 2.4 seconds to 1.7 seconds in a synthetic load test, but reviewers now complain that the page occasionally hangs for 18 seconds. What would you investigate before calling the change an improvement?"
>
> Half-right answer: "The average is lower, so the new stack is faster. I would add another GPU if people still complain."

An average can be accurate and still be a poor description of a person waiting for a response. If 99 out of 100 requests complete in one second and one takes 20 seconds, the mean is only 1.19 seconds. The one slow request is still the moment a reviewer remembers. **p99 latency** is the value below which 99% of observed requests finish; it makes that long tail visible. p50 shows a typical request, p95 shows a busy-day edge, and p99 asks whether the system remains usable when the queue, cache, model, or dependency is least forgiving.

## Trace the request, not only the model

Split end-to-end time into stages: request admission, queue wait, retrieval or feature lookup, prompt assembly, model first-token time, token generation, post-processing, and response delivery. A lower model-generation average can coexist with a worse p99 if a shared retrieval call occasionally stalls, a small batch waits to fill, a cache miss triggers a slow path, or a worker pool becomes saturated. Include errors, timeouts, cancellations, and retries rather than removing them from the chart; excluding the hardest requests makes a neat report but gives the wrong release decision.

Capacity is not a single machine count. It is the relationship among arrival rate, service time, concurrency, queue depth, payload size, and downstream limits. When utilization approaches saturation, a small increase in arrivals can produce a large increase in waiting time. A GPU might help a compute-bound model stage, but it cannot repair a serial permission check, a slow vector store, an over-long prompt, or clients retrying a request that is already in progress.

Think of two supermarket checkouts. One has a slightly quicker average because it lets many shoppers queue behind a single complicated return. Most people move quickly, but the unlucky shopper behind the return waits a long time. Adding a faster scanner does not fix the return desk. You first need to see where the line forms.

## A practical investigation path

1. Fix a synthetic workload with small, medium, and intentionally awkward requests. Record the arrival pattern, concurrency, payload bucket, cache state, and model/serving versions.
2. Report p50, p95, p99, timeout rate, cancellation rate, queue wait, and first-token versus full-response latency for the old and candidate paths. Segment rather than hide: cache hit/miss, short/long context, normal/peak load, and successful/failed request.
3. Add a trace ID to every stage. For the slowest fixed cases, inspect the stage waterfall before changing hardware.
4. Set a release gate such as: candidate must not worsen p99 or timeout rate for the agreed workload, and must remain below a stated queue-depth limit. Keep the prior path available as a safe baseline.
5. Run a limited shadow or canary comparison only with synthetic traffic in this portfolio exercise. Roll back if the tail guardrail fails, even when the average improves.

## Where an answer goes thin

"We will optimize the model" is not a diagnosis. It treats every delay as compute and skips the user-facing consequence of a tail. The simpler baseline may be a smaller prompt, lower concurrency, a cached approved template, or an asynchronous draft with a visible status indicator. Use a more complex serving engine only after traces show which stage is actually the bottleneck and the expected workload justifies its operating cost.

## Technical judgement to demonstrate

- For each workload slice, record queue wait, time-to-first-token, full-response time, errors, and cancellations. Join admission, retrieval, model, and delivery with a trace ID; use p50/p95/p99 to inspect the tail instead of reporting only average latency.
- A capacity experiment that changes one factor at a time and preserves the exact synthetic request set.

## Delivery, business, and risk judgement to demonstrate

- A named user workflow and a latency budget tied to a decision, rather than an arbitrary dashboard target.
- A release gate that protects the tail, plus a rollback route and a clear owner for interpreting regressions.
- Honest scope: lower latency in a synthetic test is not proof of productivity, customer satisfaction, savings, or production capacity.

## Portfolio artefacts that make the claim checkable

Build `tail-latency-serving-lab` with:

- `fixtures/requests.jsonl` grouped by context length, cache condition, and load wave; all prompts and outputs are invented.
- `scripts/replay-load.mjs` that sends deterministic mock stages and writes a trace per request.
- `evidence/latency-report.md` with p50/p95/p99, error counts, and an annotated waterfall for the three slowest cases.
- `docs/capacity-decision.md` explaining the baseline, the selected gate, the rejected hardware-first option, and the rollback condition.
- `tests/tail-guardrail.test.ts` that fails when a candidate improves the mean but worsens the agreed p99 threshold.

The strongest demo is a counterexample: a candidate with a better mean but a failed p99 gate. It shows that you can decline an attractive metric when it makes the workflow less dependable.

## Further reading

[Trace p99 latency before adding GPUs](/en/interview-lab/trace-p99-latency-before-adding-gpus), [build a practical AI system](/en/articles/build-an-ai-engineering-mental-model), and [review a coding-agent build without being a developer](/en/articles/review-a-coding-agent-build-without-being-a-developer).

## Scope note

This is an AI.DOG practice prompt. The service, reviewers, traces, requests, thresholds, and results are fictional synthetic local-draft material. It makes no claim about a company, a live model, production performance, or business impact.
body.zh-HK:
> 面試官問："一隊人為 internal draft assistant 換咗 serving stack。synthetic load test 的 mean latency 由 2.4 秒跌到 1.7 秒，但 reviewer 話個頁間中會卡足 18 秒。未叫它做改進之前，你會查乜？"
>
> 答啱一半嘅答案："平均值低咗，即係新 stack 較快；仲有人投訴就加 GPU。"

Average 可以係真，但未必講到一個人等回覆時的感受。如果 100 個 request 裡 99 個一秒完成，一個要 20 秒，mean 仍然只係 1.19 秒；但嗰位等緊的人只會記得 20 秒。**p99 latency** 係 99% request 會喺其內完成的時間，令長尾現形。p50 看典型 request，p95 看忙碌日邊緣，p99 則問：queue、cache、model 或 dependency 最唔順時，系統仲用唔用得？

## 追一條 request，而唔係淨係睇 model

將 end-to-end 時間拆開：request admission、queue wait、retrieval／feature lookup、prompt assembly、model first-token、token generation、post-processing、response delivery。model 平均 generation 較快，p99 一樣可以變差：shared retrieval 偶爾卡住、小 batch 等湊夠、cache miss 入咗慢路徑、worker pool 飽和。error、timeout、cancel、retry 不應從圖表刪走；拎走最難的 request 會令報告靚咗，但 release 決定錯咗。

Capacity 唔係單一機器數目，而係 arrival rate、service time、concurrency、queue depth、payload size、下游 limit 的關係。利用率接近飽和時，少少 arrival 增加都會大幅拉長等待。GPU 可能幫到 compute-bound model stage，卻修唔到 serial permission check、慢 vector store、過長 prompt，或者 client 重試一個其實正在處理的 request。

想像超市兩條收銀隊。其中一條平均快少少，因為大部分人掃完就走；但剛好有個複雜退貨，後面那個人要等很久。加快 scanner 速度唔會修好退貨檯，先要見到隊伍究竟塞喺邊。

## 一條可落地的調查路徑

1. 固定一組 synthetic workload：短、中、刻意麻煩的 request；記 arrival pattern、concurrency、payload bucket、cache state、model／serving version。
2. 為舊路徑和 candidate 報 p50、p95、p99、timeout rate、cancellation rate、queue wait、first-token 同 full-response latency。分段而唔係遮掩：cache hit/miss、短／長 context、normal／peak load、成功／失敗。
3. 每段帶 trace ID；先睇最慢固定 cases 的 stage waterfall，先好改 hardware。
4. 訂 release gate，例如 candidate 在指定 workload 下不可惡化 p99 或 timeout rate，亦不可超過 queue-depth limit；保留舊路徑做安全 baseline。
5. 呢個 portfolio 練習只用 synthetic traffic 做有限 shadow／canary；tail guardrail 失敗就 rollback，即使 average 改善。

## 答案容易變薄嘅地方

「我們會 optimize model」唔係 diagnosis。它假設所有 delay 都係 compute，跳過長尾如何妨礙用家。簡單 baseline 可能係縮短 prompt、降低 concurrency、cache 一個批准 template，或者用有狀態提示的 async draft。只有 trace 證明 bottleneck 喺邊、工作量又值得，先上複雜 serving engine。

## 呢個答案要展示嘅技術判斷

- 按 workload slice 記每條 request 的 queue wait、time-to-first-token、full-response time、error／cancel；用 trace ID 串起 admission、retrieval、model 和 delivery，並以 p50/p95/p99 睇長尾，而唔係淨係報 average latency。
- 一次只改一個 factor 的 capacity experiment，並保留同一組 synthetic request。

## 呢個答案要展示嘅交付、業務與風險判斷

- 有命名 user workflow，latency budget 對應一個決定，而唔係任意 dashboard target。
- 保護 tail 的 release gate、rollback route，及解讀 regression 的清楚 owner。
- 誠實範圍：synthetic test 較快不等於證明 productivity、customer satisfaction、節省或 production capacity。

## 可以放進 portfolio 的可檢查 artefact

建立 `tail-latency-serving-lab`：

- `fixtures/requests.jsonl`：按 context length、cache condition、load wave 分組，全部 prompt/output 都係虛構。
- `scripts/replay-load.mjs`：送 deterministic mock stages，為每個 request 寫 trace。
- `evidence/latency-report.md`：p50/p95/p99、error count、三個最慢 case 的註解 waterfall。
- `docs/capacity-decision.md`：baseline、選定 gate、被否決的 hardware-first option、rollback condition。
- `tests/tail-guardrail.test.ts`：candidate mean 改善但 p99 超標時 fail。

最有力的 demo 係 counterexample：candidate 平均更好，卻過唔到 p99 gate。它證明你會拒絕一個好看的 metric，當它令 workflow 更唔可靠。

## 延伸閱讀

[加 GPU 前先 trace p99 latency](/zh-HK/interview-lab/trace-p99-latency-before-adding-gpus)、[建立實用 AI system，而不只是 demo](/zh-HK/articles/build-an-ai-engineering-mental-model) 和 [如何審閱 coding agent 交出的 build](/zh-HK/articles/review-a-coding-agent-build-without-being-a-developer)。

## 範圍說明

這是 AI.DOG 的單題練習。service、reviewer、trace、request、threshold 和結果均為虛構 synthetic 本地草稿材料；不聲稱任何公司、live model、production performance 或商業影響。
